etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English visioun, from Anglo-Norman visioun, from Old French vision, from Latin vīsiō (“vision, seeing”), noun of action from the perfect passive participle visus (“that which is seen”), from the verb videō (“I see”) + action noun suffix -iō.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) The sense or ability of sight.
(countable) Something seen; an object perceived visually.

quote.citation: c. 1610–1611 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Winters Tale”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act I, scene ii]:
quote.text: […] For to a Viſion ſo apparant, Rumor / Cannot be mute […]

quote.citation: 1892, James Yoxall, chapter 7, in The Lonely Pyramid:
quote.text: It was the Lost Oasis, the Oasis of the vision in the sand. […] Deep-hidden in the hollow, beneath the cliffs, it lay; and round it the happy verdure spread for many a rood. […] Yes, the quest was ended, the Lost Oasis was the Found!

definitions.definition: (countable) Something imaginary one thinks one sees.

quote.citation: 2005, Elisabeth Kübler-Ross, David Kessler, On Grief and Grieving, →ISBN, page 107:
quote.text: Visitations are a commonly reported afterlife phenomenon. For example, a dying patient has a vision of her mother, who has been dead for twenty years.

definitions.definition: (countable, by extension) Something unreal or imaginary; a creation of fancy.

quote.citation: 1690, John Locke, “Of our Knowledge of the Existence of other Things”, in An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, volume II, London: A. Bettesworth et al., published 1735, book III, page 250:
quote.text: For having the Idea of any thing in our Mind, no more proves the Exiſtence of that Thing, than the Picture of a Man evidences his being in the World, or the Viſions of a Dream make thereby a true Hiſtory.

definitions.definition: (countable) An ideal or a goal toward which one aspires.
(countable) A religious or mystical experience of a supernatural appearance.
(countable) A person or thing of extraordinary beauty.
(transitive) To imagine something as if it were to be true.
(transitive) To present as in a vision.
(transitive) To provide with a vision. (Can we add an example for this sense?)
